title: Fictional federal claim against the Town of Gamma, entity capacity

parent.objective: Maintain a source-pinned claim matrix for one fictional federal claim against a municipality on a policy-or-custom theory.
parent.milestone: Claim matrix declared, custom theory stated, and governing, adverse and custom evidence read

goal: State the fictional claim's elements, entity-liability theory, threshold defense, adverse authority, remedy, limitations and justiciability.
non_goals: Predict the outcome of any claim or defense.
File, serve, or send anything to any person or court.

allowed: Declare the claim matrix and check every cited source resolves.
Record primary-source reviews of authority and of the stop log.
prohibited: Cite a real statute, case, party, or authority.
Treat an allegation as fact before a bound primary-source review.
Treat the municipality as liable for an employee's act without a policy-or-custom theory.

assertions.assertion: The fictional Town of Gamma employed Officer Alpha on 2026-01-10.
Under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 4, a municipality is liable only for a deprivation caused by its own policy or custom.
A Town of Gamma officer detained the plaintiff for forty minutes without a warrant on 2026-01-10.
Town of Gamma officers routinely held stopped drivers for over thirty minutes without a warrant during 2025.
Fictional Poe v. Town of Delta holds that a handful of prior incidents does not establish a municipal custom.
Fictional Synthetic Limitations Code section 2 sets a three-year period for this claim.
The claim accrued on the fictional stop date, 2026-01-10.
Under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 3, a person injured by a completed detention may seek damages.
The plaintiff lost a day's wages because of the detention.

claims.statement: The Town of Gamma, as an entity, caused the plaintiff's warrantless detention through a custom of prolonged stops.
claims.legal_question: Does a fictional custom of prolonged warrantless stops make the Town of Gamma liable under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 4?
claims.right: Fictional right against unreasonable seizure, on a municipal custom theory (a stand-in that states no real constitutional holding).

elements.requirement: A deprivation of a protected right.
A municipal custom that caused the deprivation.

threshold_defenses.defense: Too few prior incidents to plead a custom under fictional Poe v. Town of Delta.
threshold_defenses.rebuttal: The fictional stop log shows a pattern throughout 2025, not a handful of incidents.

remedies.description: Lost wages for the day of the fictional detention.

limitations.prerequisites: No fictional notice or exhaustion prerequisite is declared for this claim in this worked example.

justiciability.standing: A completed fictional detention with a claimed wage loss, traceable to the Town's custom and redressable by damages.
justiciability.mootness_and_prospective_relief: Damages only; no prospective relief is sought, so mootness does not arise.

entity_liability.summary: A fictional custom of prolonged warrantless stops, shown by the Town's own stop log.

claims.next_action: Have a non-implementer review the fictional stop log for the 2025 pattern.
